title: chat-server: MemoryBackend has no mention_broadcast gate
description: MemoryBackend inherits ChatBackend::may_broadcast_mention's permit-all default, so a channel Message/set create or edit with broadcastMentions is never refused. Draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 (cefc217) §BroadcastMention: 'Sending a Message with a non-empty broadcastMentions array requires the "mention_broadcast" Space permission. Servers MUST reject Message/set create or update requests that would write a broadcast mention from a sender lacking this permission with forbidden.' The reference impl should check mention_broadcast against the owner's member entry (accountId) in the channel's Space, as the other gates do since JMAP-yt1w.33. Found while fixing JMAP-yt1w.33; src/message.rs unit tests and tests/message_broadcast_permission.rs currently rely on the permissive default.
notes:
Fix implemented (uncommitted): MemoryBackend::may_broadcast_mention checks permissions::MENTION_BROADCAST (new const) against account_id's effective perms in the Space; missing Space permits. src/message.rs make_channel_chat fixture role now grants mention_broadcast. Gates: fmt, clippy, test chat-server+testjig, doc all pass.
Done in e5eddc27: tests create_in_channel_without_mention_broadcast_is_forbidden, update_retaining_broadcast_without_mention_broadcast_is_forbidden, update_adding_broadcast_without_mention_broadcast_is_forbidden; changed existing tests: broadcast_mention_create_in_channel_succeeds, broadcast_mention_update_retaining_broadcast_succeeds (shared fixture make_channel_chat), module doc only (no test logic changed)
